text:
sam: FYI — noticed sustained pcie error spike on us-west1 GPU shelf A3. Latency SLOs for a handful of tenants are creeping up. suspect noisy tenant running heavy sparse-attn jobs. can we do a quick staggered drain and route dedicated customers to reserve lanes? :rotating_light:

maria: Confirmed, dashboards show tail latency +120% for the last 10m. Metrics: pcie_uncorrectable up, HBM evictions increased. We should avoid a big simultaneous drain — causes cold-start penalties. Staggering sounds right.

lee: Agreed. If we drain too many nodes at once we blow warm-pool and increase token-cost. Proposal: drain in 5-node batches with 3m gap, keep warm-pool target at 15% for the region.

anita: For dedicated pools we can temporarily shift routing weight to reserve slices in eu-west1 (if latency delta acceptable) or fall back to quantized variant v1-q4 for less memory pressure. Which customers can tolerate cross-region?

sam: Only non-enterprise dev tenants are OK to cross-region. Enterprise/dedicated must stay in-region — we have reserved slices that can absorb ~8 concurrent reservations.

maria: Plan outline: (1) identify top-5 noisy allocations (by pcie errors & token rate), (2) throttle those allocations by 2x backoff, (3) if still noisy, soft-drain their node in batches, (4) route affected dev tenants to eu-west1 or v1-q4. I've opened the runbook.

anita: Share runbook link?

maria: ops-bot:runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-noisy-neighbor — handles detection -> staged-drain -> routing weights.

ops-bot: runbook opened: gpu-noisy-neighbor (v2). Notified oncall. Next step: sam to list candidate nodes for first drain.

sam: Candidate nodes (shortlist): usw1-gpu-a3-012, usw1-gpu-a3-014, usw1-gpu-a3-019, usw1-gpu-b1-002, usw1-gpu-b1-005. We'll start with a3-012 -> pause new allocs, wait 180s, then cordon and evacuate non-dedicated.

lee: Adding a note: update routing policy to prefer same-az reserve lanes for dedicated customers. patch in-flight in routing-service: 6950001200. Keep an eye on circuit breakers for cross-region egress.

anita: Cost note — shifting 20% of dev traffic to eu-west1 increases egress+vm premium by ~12% for the window. We should set a TTL for the cross-region fallback (max 30m) and use batch-level tagging to avoid long tails.

sam: Agreed on TTL. Also let's avoid preempting any Dedicated reservations — only soft-drain non-reserved workloads. Use the following k8s drain options on the node:

sam: ```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m
```

maria: I'll run a throttling policy first to give the noisy tenant a chance: set request token rate limit to 60% of current for 5m, escalate if metrics don't improve.

lee: If pcie_err persists after two batches, fallback: enable cache-only serving for affected tenants (no KV populate) to reduce HBM churn. That reduces quality for a subset but keeps latency stable. Notify owners.

anita: I'm running a preflight on the drain script to ensure autoscaler won't overreact and tear down warm-pool. will report back in ~4m.

ops-bot: oncall: maria_sre notified. deployments: routing-service patch queued (6950001200).

maria: Quick status update: after throttling top allocation, pcie_uncorrectable dropped ~45% in 90s. tail latency down ~30%. Holding before first drain.

sam: Good. Hold the drain for now, continue throttling + telemetry. If we can avoid node moves we save ~3-5% per-token cost this hour. :thumbsup:

lee: I'll still keep the drain playbook ready, but yeah prefer throttling+cache-only. If you want, I can flip the route weights to reserve lanes in 10m as a cold-start test.

anita: Preflight complete — autoscaler respects node annotation "no-warmscale" so warm-pool safe.

sam: Perfect. Let's re-evaluate in 10m. Thanks all.

maria: noting for postmortem: consider adding a noisy-tenant auto-throttle rule that kicks in before we need drain. Low-effort win for cost + stability.

lee: +1. Also track which model variants caused highest HBM churn — could be a model-level recommendation in Optimize.

anita: Will open a follow-up ticket to add a scheduler hint to prefer reserve slices for heavy-IO jobs.

sam: Filed follow-up: infra#1827 — scheduler hints + noisy-tenant auto-throttle. Closing thread for action: throttling in place, drain on standby. :eyes:
